prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1037; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a low-speed collision in a parking lot with another vehicle backing out of a space. The claimant was identified as the driver of the other vehicle and is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office. Verified that the driver is named on the policy.

Entry 2: Obtained the statements from the claimant's attorney and reviewed the scene photos submitted with the first notice of loss. The damage visible on both vehicles lines up with the impact described, and the rear bumper deformation is consistent with the reported speed.

Entry 3: Spoke with the two witnesses listed on the report. Both independently described the same sequence of movement and contact, and neither had any connection to either party.

Entry 4: Took the other driver's recorded statement. Their account of the collision matches the witnesses and the photos in every material respect.

Entry 5: Received the medical records from the claimant's treating provider. The reported back strain fits the kind and force of the impact. Treatment followed a usual course, with physical therapy tapering off as the patient improved. The records also note a small strain in the same area several years ago that healed fully.

Entry 6: Spoke with the claimant through counsel. The account given was the same as in the first notice of loss and in every later conversation. It is not yet fully clear from the file where in the vehicle the claimant was seated at the moment of impact, so I have requested a seating description and a follow-up interview.

Entry 7: Checked the vehicle history and prior claim records. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on file. A neighbor who was contacted informally believes the car had been damaged several weeks before the stated loss date, but that remains an unverified recollection and has not been confirmed by any document or other witness.

Entry 8: Reviewed the damage estimate against the impact photos and the reported point of contact. The repair scope matches the described impact, and no additional areas of damage were identified during reinspection.

Entry 9: Summarized the file for supervisor review. Liability and the accident itself are supported by witnesses, photos, and the other driver's account. Outstanding items are the seating position question and the neighbor's recollection about prior damage, which will be followed up with counsel before any settlement evaluation.
